rationale: Sell 10 percent of the spot book at 86,266.8 - about 0.00021389 BTC, roughly 18.45 USDT - and carry the remaining 90 percent through the overnight gap behind a resting stop at 84,650.0. This is a risk-management trim, not a directional call, and it is sized so it cannot be either. Three facts set it up. FIRST, the calendar: this is the last report of the day and the next mark is roughly six hours away on the far side of the thinnest books of the week, with a daily Wilder ATR(14) of 2,562.85 - one average day of range from here lands at 83,703.9, which is almost exactly where midday's old reduce gate sat, so an unmanaged book is one ordinary overnight session away from giving back the whole breakout. SECOND, the tape said no at 87,399.0: that eight-month high was rejected by 1,132.2 points into the close, 4H RSI is 86.43 - the highest reading in the entire 299-bar series and 3.72 points above the 82.71 midday already called extreme - the 15m MACD histogram is negative at minus 74.83, and price has slipped below its own 15m EMA20 at 86,470.8. THIRD, and this is the one that decided the sizing rather than the direction: open interest is 2,564,275,351 USD, DOWN 3.35 percent from midday's 2,653,274,142 while price rose 0.42 percent. Rising price on falling open interest is short covering, not fresh long demand, so the fuel behind the last leg has already been spent and does not regenerate while nobody is watching. Against all of that sits the strongest single fact of the day, and it is why this is a 10 percent trim and not a 30 percent one: Farside now prints plus 617.6 million USD of US spot-ETF inflow for 21 September, the largest of the month and a third consecutive positive day worth plus 1,210.1 million - the allocation confirmation midday named as the datapoint that would settle whether this break was real. Positioning also argues against a flush: the OKX long/short account ratio is 0.93 and falling, so accounts are still net short into strength, and funding for the 08:00 UTC settlement is plus 0.0001, the practical floor, so no long premium is being paid. Deliberately NOT opening futures: taking leverage into a 300-bar RSI extreme, inside an 86,250.0-86,750.0 band where 559,000 USD of longs AND shorts were liquidated in the same four-hour window, is paying the worst possible price for the best-known story. The 18 USDT this raises takes cash to roughly 49 and funds the 85,600.0 retest the report names as its add gate - which is the reserve the morning lesson said to keep and the morning session did not have.

message.text: BTC closed the day at 86,266.8 after printing 87,399.0, the highest since 29 January 2026, and fading 1,132.2 points off it. I trimmed 10 percent of the spot book at 86,266.8 - risk management for the overnight gap, not a top call - and left 90 percent running. Cash is now around 49 USDT, deliberately, so you can act rather than watch. Read it this way. Three settled 4H bodies now sit above the old 85,631.3 January ceiling (85,931.7, 86,502.3, 86,617.8), so that shelf is FLIP SUPPORT and the breakout is a structure, not a candle. The overnight chop band is 86,250.0 to 86,750.0: both sides of it were liquidated inside the same four-hour window, 189,548 USD of longs and 164,934 USD of shorts in the 86,500.0 bucket alone, so expect it to pay nobody. My add gate is 85,600.0 holding on a settled 1H close - that is the base the final leg launched from and it is where the cash I just raised belongs. Reduce on a settled 1H close below 85,325.2. Invalidation is 84,719.5, today's low; a resting stop sits at 84,650.0. Do NOT chase above 86,750.0 on momentum alone: 4H RSI is 86.43, the highest in 299 bars, and open interest FELL 3.35 percent while price rose, which means the last leg was shorts closing, not longs building. The one fact that would justify you being aggressive is the ETF tape - plus 617.6 million USD on 21 September, third straight positive day, plus 1,210.1 million on the streak. If Asia holds 86,300.0 with that flow behind it, the retest add is the trade. If we open under 85,325.2, you are the seeder for a different day.

lesson.pattern: Three sessions in one day each faced the same question - press, hold, or bank - at 84,742.7, 85,904.7 and 86,266.8, and the results split by WHY each acted rather than by which direction they chose. Morning trimmed on an oscillator reading alone and lost 1,524.1 points. Midday added because a pre-committed price gate filled and gained 362.1. This session banks a small slice because a measurable structural fact changed - open interest fell 3.35 percent while price rose, so the buyer of last resort left the perpetual.
lesson.insight: Grade a decision by the class of evidence behind it, not by the direction it took. A momentum oscillator at an extreme tells you the pace is unusual, nothing about the turn - it is a sizing input, never a trigger. A price level you wrote down in advance, or a positioning series you can measure twice and compare, is a trigger. When the only thing arguing for action is an indicator, shrink the size to the point where being wrong is noise; when a structural fact changes, act on it but keep the core, because structure changes slowly and one datapoint is not a trend.
